Apple Watch Battery Life Tips
articles.summary: To conserve battery life on an Apple Watch, users can check its battery health status and adjust their usage patterns, including enabling Low Power Mode to extend battery life by several days.
articles.content: Apple Watch users often find themselves struggling to squeeze out every last bit of battery life from their device, especially on days when they need it most. The company claims that its latest models can last for up to 24 hours on a single charge, but real-world results often vary greatly depending on individual usage patterns. Apple's own estimates are based on a combination of 300 time checks, 15 minutes of app use, six hours of sleep tracking, and other factors. To give your Apple Watch an extra boost, it's worth checking its battery health status to see if it's still performing within normal parameters. You can do this by navigating to Settings > Battery > Battery Health on your watch. If you find that your Apple Watch's battery life is significantly depleted, it may be time to consider bringing it in for a replacement. However, power users might prefer to opt for the Apple Watch Ultra 4, which boasts a larger battery and is better equipped to handle demanding usage. Making small adjustments to how you use your watch throughout the day can also help eke out more battery life. This includes enabling certain toggles and being mindful of your app usage and other power-hungry features. When your Apple Watch's battery life starts to dwindle, turning on Low Power Mode can be a lifesaver. To activate this feature, press the side button and tap on the battery percentage in the top right corner of the screen. A notification will appear with an information card that provides instructions for enabling Low Power Mode. Scroll down and select "Turn On" to proceed, or choose to keep the mode active for one, two, or three days if you anticipate being away from a charger during that time. Alternatively, you can access Low Power Mode by navigating to Settings > Battery on your Apple Watch. This will allow you to toggle the feature on and off as needed. When Low Power Mode is activated, several changes become apparent immediately. The Always On display is disabled, along with the Wrist Flick and Double Tap gestures. However, your watch's screen will still light up automatically when you raise your wrist. Background heart rate and blood oxygen measurements are paused while in Low Power Mode, but you can use their respective apps to take manual readings at any time. This does mean that low, high, or irregular heart rate notifications will be disabled, which may be a concern for some users. Apple notes that Siri requests on the Apple Watch can take longer to process when the device is running in Low Power Mode. Additionally, Live Activities and complications on your watch face will update less frequently, and scrolling may become slightly more sluggish as a result. When using your Apple Watch in areas with Wi-Fi connectivity, it's a good idea to opt for this internet connection instead of relying on cellular data. This is because connecting to Wi-Fi can help conserve battery life, which is especially useful when you're not actively using the watch. However, if you do need to use cellular connectivity, make sure your Apple Watch and iPhone are connected. A tiny green phone icon in Control Center on your Apple Watch indicates that this connection has been established over Bluetooth. To further extend your Apple Watch's battery life, consider enabling Airplane Mode when you're not actively using the device for an extended period. This can be found in either Control Center or through the Settings app. Despite the limitations of being disconnected from the internet, your Apple Watch still offers a range of features that don't require online access. These include tracking workouts, playing stored music or podcasts, making purchases with Apple Pay and monitoring sleep patterns. The built-in apps on your Apple Watch also continue to function as usual when offline. This includes Alarms, Timers, Medications and Voice Memos, among others. Newer Apple Watch models come equipped with improved speakers that allow for direct music playback, while companion app installations on the watch are automatically synced from the paired iPhone if available. The convenience of having multiple apps installed on your Apple Watch comes at a cost - battery life. To conserve power, it's essential to manage app usage and notifications effectively. Uninstalling unused apps from your watch directly doesn't remove them from your iPhone, so consider deleting them from the watch if you're not using them frequently. For occasional use apps that don't require constant updates, turn off Background App Refresh by navigating to Settings > General > Background App Refresh. Disabling Background App Refresh entirely will affect all apps on your watch, but this might be a necessary step to save battery life. If you're unsure which apps are consuming the most power, monitoring their usage can help identify areas for improvement. Customizing app notifications is another way to reduce battery drain. By default, disabled iPhone app notifications also apply to your Apple Watch, but you can adjust this setting through the Watch app on your iPhone. To fine-tune notification settings, navigate to Notifications in the Watch app and scroll down to the Mirror iPhone Alerts From section. Disable toggles for apps that don't need to send notifications to your watch, reducing vibrations and screen wake-ups throughout the day. Turning off Always On display is another option for those seeking more control over battery life. To do this, navigate to Settings > Display & Brightness > Always On on your Apple Watch and toggle the feature off. Covering your Apple Watch when not in use is a simple yet effective way to minimize screen-on time and save battery life. This habit can be developed by making it a point to always use your palm to cover the watch face after you've finished interacting with it. Another option worth exploring is disabling the Always On display, which can have a significant impact on battery life. According to testing, turning off this feature can extend battery life by 10 to 12 hours. This setting is located in the Display & Brightness menu within Settings. Preventing accidental screen activation is also crucial for conserving battery power. To do this, navigate to Settings > Gestures and toggle off Wake on Wrist Raise. Additionally, disabling gestures like Double Tap and Wrist Flick can help reduce unnecessary screen time. For users who regularly engage in longer workouts, configuring Low Power Mode to only kick in during specific exercises can be a viable option. This feature allows you to sacrifice some workout tracking features in exchange for extended battery life. In watchOS 27, the Workout app introduced two new options that enable this functionality. To take advantage of these options, open the Workout app and select an activity type. Tap on the Goals and Targets button in the top-right corner, then scroll down and tap on Extended to start tracking your activity with reduced features. Some workouts also offer a Max Extended Workout option, which further reduces GPS and heart rate measurements. This approach can help you strike a balance between workout tracking and battery conservation. Once you've completed an exercise, Low Power Mode will automatically turn off, allowing your watch to return to normal functionality. To activate automatic battery saver mode during workouts, head to Settings > Workout and toggle on Low Power Mode. This feature eliminates the need for manual selection of Extended Workout each time. With Low Power Mode activated, your Apple Watch will automatically switch to this setting once you've begun a workout, saving precious battery life. Once an exercise is completed, the watch returns to normal functionality, allowing for uninterrupted use until the next workout. articles.content: Manchester United's new head coach Mauricio Pochettino has had his baptism by fire after just one match in charge, and it's clear he knows what challenges lie ahead. Speaking at his first press conference, he hinted at a desire to take the team to a "different place". The initial 15 minutes of Pochettino's tenure were promising, but that optimism was short-lived as Liverpool quickly took control, leaving United's defense exposed and vulnerable. The visitors' ferocity proved too much for the home team, who struggled to cope with the pace and intensity of the game. Manchester United had been expected to pick up where they left off under Michael Carrick, but Pochettino's appointment brought a sense of calm and stability to the club. With his Premier League experience and track record of delivering results, there was little reason to believe that the team would struggle under his leadership. The underlying statistics suggested that United were a mid-table team, neither significantly better nor worse than average in terms of expected goals. However, that's not enough to guarantee success, especially against a team as strong as Liverpool. Pochettino will now face the task of addressing the team's defensive vulnerabilities and finding ways to improve their performance out of possession. With a steep learning curve ahead, he'll be hoping that his players can adapt quickly to his new approach and avoid a relegation battle. The gulf between Manchester United's aspirations and their current reality is starkly illustrated by their collapse against Liverpool. The team's inability to cope with a red card has been a recurring theme this season, and it's clear that they are struggling to adapt to the demands of the Premier League. Leny Yoro's mistake in allowing Alexander Isak to earn his team a penalty was compounded by his decision to stay on the pitch despite being given a yellow card. This error of judgment gave Liverpool a significant advantage, and Dominik Szoboszlai made the most of it with a powerful free kick that left United reeling. The introduction of Harry Maguire to marshal a back five was a belated attempt to stem the bleeding, but it ultimately proved insufficient to prevent the scoreline from being further extended. In the final 25 minutes of the game, Ngumoha and Victor Munoz added two more goals to Liverpool's tally, leaving United with a humiliating defeat. The fact that Pochettino was able to recognize the need for an adjustment in his team's strategy after the red card is a testament to his tactical acumen. However, it's clear that he has a lot of work to do to turn this team around and prevent them from being embroiled in a relegation battle. The manner in which United were dismantled by Liverpool raises serious questions about their ability to compete at the highest level. With their current form, they are in danger of becoming embroiled in a relegation battle, and Pochettino will be under pressure to turn things around quickly. The defensive woes of Manchester United are well-documented, but the latest defeat at Liverpool has highlighted the extent of the problem. A team that is struggling to keep pace with its opponents has a midfield that lacks dynamism and a defense that is woefully short on athleticism. Lisandro Martinez's struggles at left back were particularly evident as he struggled to keep up with the pace of Bradley Barcola. The same issues have plagued United in central defense this season, where Martinez has been deployed. It's clear that his limbs are not well-suited for the demands of the position, and it's a problem that Pochettino will need to address sooner rather than later. The team's poor defensive record is not just down to individual mistakes, but also a lack of cohesion and organization. United's midfield has been a major concern all season, and the latest defeat has done nothing to change that perception. Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo have failed to make an impact in their roles, and it's hard to see how they will be able to turn things around quickly. The team needs a midfield that can dominate possession and create scoring opportunities, but currently, it lacks the quality and depth. Pochettino has already spent heavily on midfielders, including Tielemans, Carlos Baleba, and Andrey Santos, but so far, none of them have made a significant impact. This is a worrying trend for United fans, who will be hoping that Pochettino can turn things around quickly. However, the team's poor form has left it with little room for error. The defensive problems at Manchester United are not just limited to individual players, but also the lack of athleticism and pace in the team as a whole. De Ligt is struggling to adapt to the Premier League, and Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Yoro, Noussair Mazraoui, Luke Shaw, and Ayden Heaven all have their own issues. Pochettino will need to make significant changes to his squad if he wants to turn things around quickly. This could involve bringing in new defenders in January, as well as midfielders who can provide more energy and dynamism. It's a tall order, but Pochettino has a reputation for being able to get the best out of his players. Despite the latest defeat, there is still reason to be optimistic about Manchester United's prospects. The team has appointed an above-average coach in Pochettino, and with some shrewd signings in January, they could yet turn their season around. articles.title: Solar Panel Installation Costs Outweigh Benefits in Some Areas
articles.summary: Homeowners in certain regions may struggle to recoup their investment through savings on utility bills due to less favorable regulations or geography.
articles.content: The idea of adding solar panels to your home may seem like a great way to save money on electricity bills and boost the resale value of your property. However, there are several drawbacks to consider before making such an investment. These issues can be particularly pronounced for homeowners in states or regions with less favorable regulations or geography that doesn't receive optimal amounts of sunlight. In these cases, the benefits of solar panels may not outweigh the costs. The initial cost of installing a typical home solar power system is substantial, ranging from $20,000 to $27,000 before any incentives or rebates are applied. The national benchmark for this investment is $3.36 per watt, which can be a significant expense for many homeowners. Homeowners in certain areas may find that the upfront cost of installing solar panels is not justified by their electricity usage and rates. For instance, those living in states with relatively low electricity costs may struggle to recoup their investment through savings on their utility bills. The federal tax credit of 30 percent was previously available to help offset this expense, but it has been terminated by the Trump administration for now. This means that homeowners who had been counting on this incentive will need to weigh their options carefully before making a decision about solar panel installation. Homeowners in certain regions may find that installing solar panels has little effect on their electricity bills, particularly if they reside in a smaller dwelling, have a small household, or use energy-efficient appliances and consume minimal energy each month. To make an informed decision about investing in solar power, it's essential to research the incentives and rebates offered by your utility company. Not all companies provide net metering, which allows homeowners to receive credits for excess energy produced by their panels, potentially reducing or eliminating their monthly electric bill. The terms of these programs vary significantly from state to state, with some offering one-to-one power exchange, where homeowners are credited at the same retail rate they pay for electricity. Other states have buyback programs, reduced-rate structures, or net billing systems that credit homeowners a portion of what they pay for energy. When considering solar panels, geographic location is crucial. Areas with consistent sunlight and moderate temperatures tend to be ideal, as excessive heat or overcast weather can negatively impact panel performance and lifespan. The design of your home also plays a significant role in determining the feasibility of solar panels. Roofs that face south and are free from obstructions such as buildings, trees, or other objects are typically preferred for installation. If your roof is old, it may be necessary to install a new one before investing in solar panels, which can cost anywhere from $4,000 to over $35,000 depending on the size of your home and type of roof. In addition to these factors, homeowners should also consider the upfront costs associated with installing solar panels, including equipment, labor, and potential permitting fees. Homeowners considering solar panels often prioritize their visual appeal. Some may be hesitant to install traditional solar panels on a newly replaced roof, finding them unattractive and bulky. As an alternative, solar shingles are available, but they come with a hefty price tag. These shingles cost roughly twice as much per watt as standard solar panels. The installation costs for solar shingles can add up quickly, especially for larger homes. For example, installing solar shingles on a 2,500-square-foot house could cost between $52,500 and $62,500 before any available incentives are factored in. This price includes the cost of equipment, labor, and potential permitting fees. Another factor to consider is the reliability of solar power during outages. Many homeowners assume that their solar panels will automatically kick into gear when the grid goes down. However, this isn't the case without a battery backup system. These systems store excess energy generated by the solar panels and supply it to the home when needed. The cost of a single-battery backup system can be steep, ranging from $10,000 to $16,000 for basic models that power essential appliances like lights and refrigerators. More comprehensive multi-battery backups, capable of powering entire homes, come with an even higher price tag: between $22,000 and $40,000. In addition to maintenance costs, these battery backup systems require regular upkeep to ensure they function properly during outages. Homeowners should factor in these ongoing expenses when calculating the total cost of a solar panel system. When selling a home with solar panels, there's an added layer of complexity that buyers must consider. The presence of outstanding financing or power purchase agreements can be a major deterrent for potential buyers who don't want to take on the associated costs and responsibilities. This is because prospective buyers may view the unpaid balance as a liability, potentially affecting their ability to secure a mortgage or qualify for a solar lease themselves. In fact, if the buyer refuses to assume the remainder of the contract, they may be required to pay off the entire balance upfront - an expensive proposition that could derail the sale altogether. To make matters worse, buyers must also meet the leasing company's approval requirements in order to secure the necessary financing for the solar equipment. This can add significant time and paperwork to the home-buying process, with some leases taking up to two months to be approved. Ultimately, homeowners who finance their solar panels through a power purchase agreement or lease may find that they're unable to sell their property quickly or at a fair price due to these unforeseen complications. articles.title: Network Outages Leave US on Edge, Prompting Stockpiling of Supplies
articles.summary: A recent surge in network outages has led to widespread stockpiling of supplies as Americans prepare for potential disruptions.
articles.content: The recent spate of network outages has left the US on edge, prompting many Americans to stock up on supplies in anticipation of further disruptions. At a time when concerns about an impending catastrophe are running high, people are flocking to stores like Costco and Walmart to buy up essentials in bulk. The rush on supplies is reminiscent of the pandemic-era lockdowns, when grocery stores struggled to keep up with demand for basic necessities like toilet paper. In a bid to reassure the public, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton appeared on CNN's State of the Union last Sunday, where he was asked about the wisdom of stockpiling goods in preparation for extended outages. The U.S. intelligence chief's words of reassurance may not be enough to calm the nation's growing unease over widespread outages. Clayton suggested that being aware of potential disruptions and upgrades is a key part of preparing for them, rather than stockpiling goods or taking drastic measures. He pointed out that companies and governments are actively working on upgrading systems and dealing with interruptions head-on, which may be reassuring to some but not enough to alleviate concerns about the reliability of critical infrastructure. The recent spate of outages has left many wondering whether they should take steps to prepare for extended disruptions. The latest round of outages has raised questions about the resilience of critical infrastructure in the US. Despite assurances from officials that there's no evidence of coordinated attacks, concerns are growing about the vulnerability of networks to cyber threats. Reports of unpatched vulnerabilities being exploited by AI-powered hackers suggest a hasty rollout of network upgrades may have left gaps in security. In recent days, high-profile targets such as the FBI and Agriculture Department have been hit by cyberattacks. The sheer scale of these incidents has led some officials to question whether they are mere coincidence or part of a larger pattern. With the US already on edge after the launch of the FORTRESS initiative aimed at ensuring military bases can operate independently in times of crisis. The Federal Emergency Management Agency is reportedly scrambling to address concerns about the outages, with two officials admitting they find it hard to believe these incidents are unrelated. One official has taken steps to prepare for a potential emergency by stocking up on cash, while another is being bombarded by anxious inquiries from former classmates. These developments have added to the sense of unease in Washington, where one FEMA official described the situation as "scary" and lamented the lack of clear leadership. The comments underscore the unprecedented nature of the current crisis, with multiple sectors experiencing simultaneous outages for the first time in history. The UK government has been advising citizens to stockpile essential supplies in preparation for potential disruptions, recommending three days' worth of canned food, bottled water, and cash on hand. Mark Giles, director of Ookla Research, points out that the current outages are not linked, with most issues being self-contained and short-lived. However, he notes that the severity of recent events is unusual, particularly when it comes to critical services like banking and communication networks. articles.title: Power Grid Struggles to Keep Up with Data Center Demand
articles.summary: A major challenge facing the development of artificial intelligence infrastructure is the slow pace of the power grid, which is struggling to keep up with growing demand from data centers.
articles.content: The tech industry's rapid expansion is colliding with the slow pace of the power grid, creating a major challenge for the development of artificial intelligence infrastructure. According to Citigroup, Big Tech will spend more than $2.8 trillion on AI infrastructure through 2029, while a Brookings study estimates that U.S. investment in AI will reach $10.3 trillion between 2025 and 2032. The power grid is struggling to keep up with the growing demand from data centers, which are consuming an increasing share of the nation's electricity. Since 2000, power usage by data centers has risen at a rate of 19% per year, while U.S. grid capacity has expanded just 2% annually, according to Howden. The resulting mismatch in timing is creating one of the biggest bottlenecks facing the AI industry, as companies struggle to secure the necessary power supply for their operations. Furthermore, data centers are projected to take up a significant share of the nation's grid capacity, with estimates suggesting that they would need to source around 58% of their power off the grid by 2030. The issue has become even more pressing in light of recent election results, which saw voters reject data center projects almost across the board. The rejection of these projects now adds a new layer of complexity to the challenge of meeting growing demand for AI infrastructure, as politicians and policymakers grapple with the implications of this trend. The growth in demand for electricity to power data centers is outpacing the expansion of the grid by a significant margin. According to projections from Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, data centers could account for as much as 12% of U.S. electricity usage by 2028, up from just 1.9% in 2018. This rapid increase in demand has created a timing mismatch between the needs of the data center industry and the ability of the grid to supply power. Rob Gramlich, president of Grid Strategies, notes that building new grid capacity is a complex process that requires "deliberate study and planning" over several years, making it difficult for data centers to get the power they need quickly enough. The industry's lack of experience in handling large-scale growth is also contributing to the problem. After two decades of relatively stable demand, utilities have lost their expertise in building new infrastructure, leaving them struggling to keep up with the surge in data center development. As a result, many data center projects are likely to face delays, with Kathryn Burke estimating that between 50% and 60% will take longer than initially planned. The public's growing concern about grid strain and rising electricity prices has also added an extra hurdle for developers, as evidenced by the recent rejection of data center proposals in 40 out of 41 local ballot measures on November 3. The growing concern about data centers has become a contentious issue among young voters, who are more likely to oppose new data center developments in their area. A recent survey conducted by the University of Pennsylvania Annenberg Public Policy Center found that 70% of adults under 30 expressed strong opposition to new data centers in their local community. In contrast, only 61% of all adults surveyed shared this sentiment. The widespread concern is not unfounded, as many regions are struggling with the strain on their power grids caused by data centers. Northern Virginia, for instance, boasts an unusually high concentration of these facilities, while a significant portion of Virginia's electricity sales go to commercial customers, including those serving data centers. Data center growth has also been shown to have a disproportionate impact on local energy prices, as evident in studies conducted by Cornell University researchers Cheng Feng and Fengqi You. The rising demand for power by tech companies is putting pressure on local energy prices and infrastructure. This mismatch in timing between data center growth and grid expansion has significant implications for communities hosting these operations. Some states are pushing back against this trend by requiring large energy users to produce or secure 100% of the power they use, including a share of clean energy. For instance, Delaware has become the first state to enact such legislation, mandating that data centers and other major consumers meet their own energy needs within a decade. President Donald Trump's Ratepayer Protection Pledge is another example of this shift in approach. The pledge encourages signers to "build, bring, or buy new-generation resources and electricity as needed, with several major tech companies and utilities already on board. The growth in on-site generation is also noteworthy, with BloombergNEF tracking a significant increase in announced gas-fired power plants proposed alongside data centers. In fact, the research firm has counted over 181 gigawatts of such projects worldwide, with the majority located in the US. This surge in on-site energy production is likely to continue as more states and companies adopt bring your own power" models. The long-term implications for local energy markets and infrastructure will be significant, and communities hosting these operations must prepare accordingly. The rapid growth of data centers, driven by increasing demand for AI computing power, is straining the US electrical grid. According to industry experts, this mismatch in timing could lead to a surge in greenhouse gas emissions from the power sector, potentially reaching 20% higher than current levels. Data center development specialists warn that the model of building large-scale data centers and gas-fired power plants is not sustainable in the long term. The rapid fluctuations in power demand can cause outages and damage on-site generation equipment, highlighting the need for more efficient and reliable energy solutions. As lawmakers take office in January, new regulations could be on the horizon. Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has proposed a moratorium on new data center development, while Ohio is set to add to its existing 125 local data center moratoriums, underscoring the growing concern about the environmental impact of this trend. articles.title: A couple in their 50s spent $1 million building their forever home. It has a gym, pool, and aging-in-place features
articles.summary: A couple in their 50s has built their dream home, which features a gym, pool, and aging-in-place amenities.
articles.content: A couple in their 50s has built their dream home, which features a gym, pool, and aging-in-place amenities. Tony Stamper, a construction manager, and his wife Carla, a content creator, made the decision to build their forever home after realizing it would be financially feasible with the proceeds from selling their previous house and taking out a loan. The couple had long discussed building their own home, but it was only when they reached this point in their lives that it became a reality. Their youngest child was preparing for college at the time, prompting them to think about retirement and whether they wanted to move to a lower-maintenance living situation. They initially considered condos, thinking this would free up time for travel, but soon realized it wasn't suitable for their lifestyle. Carla Stamper explained that they quickly ruled out condos as an option because it didn't align with what they were looking for in a home. With their children growing older and moving away, the couple began to think about creating a space where they could age comfortably in retirement. Their plan is to retire in 2029 and beyond, which motivated them to design a home that would meet their needs as they grew older. Their vision for a forever home was clear: a place where they could live in comfort and tranquility, yet still be close enough to the city to enjoy its amenities. To achieve this balance, they needed a design that would serve them well now and in the years to come, taking into account any potential changes in their health or mobility. The Stampers' home was designed with aging-in-place features, ensuring that it could accommodate their needs as they grew older. A key aspect of their plan was incorporating ADA accommodations, not just for themselves but also for Tony's mother, who uses a wheelchair. They wanted to create a space where they could easily care for each other or have someone assist them without having to leave the house. The floor plan they chose online served as a starting point, which they then adapted and refined with the help of an architect and their own expertise. Tony's construction experience and Carla's keen eye for design allowed them to navigate the renovation process with confidence. The renovation process required some groundwork before construction could begin. The couple had to level certain areas to ensure their house would be stable and drain properly. To make the most of the property's elevation, they adjusted the original floor plan accordingly. For instance, the garage was relocated from the same level as the house to underneath it, freeing up interior living space. This change also allowed them to create a larger garage, which Tony appreciates for storing items beyond their cars. The extra storage space is a welcome addition to the property. A second driveway was added to the property, providing an alternative entrance and exit point. This feature was particularly important to the couple, who wanted to ensure accessibility for themselves and any future guests with mobility issues. The driveways were a significant investment, costing $18,000. However, the Stampers believe it's worth the expense for the convenience and peace of mind they provide. The exterior grounds are designed to be low-maintenance, which will simplify upkeep as the couple ages. This was an essential consideration in their home design. Carla had a clear vision for the interior layout of their forever home. She wanted to create an open-concept floor plan that seamlessly connected the living areas and kitchen. When entering the house, Carla's dream is realized through large glass doors overlooking the backyard. A stairway sits past the doorway, creating a cozy nook to its left. The couple's home has undergone extensive modifications to make it more accessible for Tony's mom and other family members who may need assistance in the future. In fact, all doorways on the first floor have been widened to accommodate wheelchairs or walkers, allowing easy navigation throughout the living space. Large archways connecting various rooms not only add a touch of luxury but also provide an unobstructed path for those with mobility issues. Flat thresholds on the first floor further enhance accessibility, enabling Tony's mom to move around the home without difficulty. The kitchen, one of Carla's favorite areas in the house, boasts double islands that serve as both a food preparation station and a space for entertaining guests. By opting for pre-manufactured cabinets and adding trim to give them a custom look, the Stampers were able to offset the cost of their high-end appliances. However, Tony's father, who owns Craft Interiors, a company that sells cabinets, notes that natural light could have been incorporated into the kitchen design if the cabinet layout had been different. In its place, Carla enjoys spending time in the adjacent breakfast nook, which features bench seating and large windows that let in plenty of sunlight. The Stampers' home office is cleverly disguised within the mudroom and pantry area. This space serves as a multifunctional hub, perfect for tackling various tasks and projects. Carla's decision to repurpose this area was a wise one, providing her family with a more practical layout that suits their needs. The Stampers have clearly put thought into designing their home with functionality in mind. The desk positioned within the mudroom serves as the couple's designated workspace. It's an ideal spot for tackling projects or exploring new opportunities when they choose to do so. Even in retirement, the Stampers appreciate having a dedicated space to pursue their interests and passions. This thoughtful consideration reflects their forward-thinking approach to aging-in-place design. The Stampers' bedroom is conveniently located on the first floor of their home, allowing them to live entirely on one level. This was an intentional decision made by the couple to ensure ease of mobility as they age. On the second floor of their house, the Stampers have a total of three bedrooms and a movie room that could be converted into a bedroom if needed. However, Carla and Tony's preference is to stay on the first floor. The bathroom connected to the Stampers' suite features an impressive zero-threshold doorway. This thoughtful design element allows for seamless navigation, even for visitors with mobility issues. Inside this luxurious bathroom, a stunning free-standing tub takes center stage, accompanied by an inset fireplace that adds warmth and ambiance to the space. The remnant tile used for the countertops was a cost-effective solution while still maintaining high-end aesthetics. The shower area within the Stampers' bathroom is a masterpiece of design, stretching 13 feet in length with entrances on both sides. This spacious shower features multiple nozzles, a wide bench, and built-in shelving, creating a truly luxurious experience that's also practical for users with mobility needs. The couple's forever home has a functional layout that suits their needs and preferences. A second washer-dryer unit upstairs ensures that family members or guests don't have to share laundry facilities with them. Their original floor plan would have put the garage where the gym is now located, but they opted for a more practical design. The home gym features a treadmill, weights, and a rowing machine, all situated in front of large windows offering a view of their backyard. Both homeowners consider the gym to be one of the standout features of their property. Their old house had limited space for exercise equipment, so having a dedicated room for this purpose feels like a significant upgrade. The gym also includes a sauna with a wooden interior and bench seating, which was installed by the couple themselves after they found an option that suited them online. The sauna's design blends in seamlessly with the rest of the home's aesthetic. By having their pool, gym, and sauna on one level, the homeowners can easily incorporate physical activity into their daily routines as part of their long-term health goals. A well-designed layout allows for seamless transitions between indoor and outdoor living spaces. Their home's interior design emphasizes functionality and accessibility, making it easy to move around and enjoy various amenities without strain. articles.title: Hakeem Jeffries Discusses Upcoming Role as Speaker of the House
articles.summary: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries discussed his upcoming role as Speaker of the House on "Face the Nation", highlighting key issues such as affordability and accountability.
articles.content: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, a Democrat from New York, appeared on "Face the Nation to discuss his upcoming role as Speaker of the House. He joined host Margaret Brennan from New York, marking an important moment in the lead-up to January's congressional changes. Brennan began by highlighting the key issues that voters prioritized during the recent election, citing exit polls that showed a strong focus on affordability and accountability. Specifically, 89% of respondents identified cost of living as crucial or major factors in their voting decisions. The importance of addressing corruption was also clear, with 90% of voters sharing this concern. Jeffries acknowledged these concerns, vowing to work diligently to fulfill Democratic promises related to affordability and accountability. He emphasized the need to reduce the high cost of living, stating that life is way too expensive for many Americans who are already struggling to make ends meet. The House Minority Leader emphasized the importance of reversing Medicaid cuts in order to protect vulnerable populations. Restoring SNAP benefits is also crucial to ensuring that low-income individuals have access to basic necessities like food and groceries. Bipartisanship on certain issues seems unlikely given the president's past support for Republican-led initiatives, including those related to taxes and spending. However, Jeffries remains committed to delivering bold change that aligns with the demands of the American people. The healthcare system in the United States is fundamentally flawed, requiring a comprehensive overhaul to provide better outcomes for patients. articles.summary: A recent update to Apple's iOS has brought significant changes to the way iPhones use storage space, with Apple Intelligence consuming between 8GB and 14GB of room on different iPhone models.
articles.content: A recent update to Apple's iOS has brought significant changes to the way iPhones use storage space. One of the key features affected is Apple Intelligence, which now takes up a substantial amount of room on devices. The new requirements for Apple Intelligence have left some users wondering about their storage capacity. The feature reportedly consumes between 8GB and 14GB of space on different iPhone models, leaving those with limited storage struggling to make ends meet. This can be particularly challenging for individuals who rely on their iPhones as primary devices. Users who are not interested in utilizing Apple Intelligence's features or prefer to conserve storage space have been seeking ways to reclaim the lost capacity. Fortunately, there is a method available that allows users to recover some of this space, albeit it requires more effort than simply disabling individual features. The exact amount of storage required for Apple Intelligence varies across iPhone models. According to official guidelines from Apple, devices such as the iPhone Duo, iPhone Air, and iPhone 17 Pro or later require up to 14GB for the feature's functionality. In contrast, other compatible iPhone models need around 8GB of space. Disabling Apple Intelligence in iOS 27 has become a more complex process compared to previous versions of the operating system. Even after turning off the various features that comprise Apple Intelligence, the system retains them, ready to be reactivated if needed. To reclaim storage space on an iPhone, users need to make some adjustments to Siri's language settings without changing their phone's default language. Go to Settings and navigate to the Siri section, where you can select Language from a list of options. Choosing a different variation of English, such as English (Canada), should allow you to see the saved storage space after restarting your iPhone. This workaround may not be stable in future software updates, so users are advised to exercise caution when implementing this solution. The loss of Apple Intelligence features can have significant impacts on an iPhone's functionality, particularly with Siri. When turned off, Siri loses its contextual understanding capabilities and ability to perform actions within other apps, reverting to a more basic level of interaction. Additionally, the camera app will no longer have access to Siri mode, which provides information about objects or scenes captured by the lens. iOS 27 allows users to selectively toggle Apple Intelligence tools on or off. Several Apple apps have been upgraded with AI-driven capabilities in addition to the core Apple Intelligence features on your iPhone. The Photos app now boasts enhanced image cleanup functionality, while Safari will automatically organize your tabs by topic for easier browsing. These new features can be quite useful, but they also require consideration of storage space taken up by Apple Intelligence. As you navigate these upgrades, it ultimately comes down to weighing the importance of available space against the convenience offered by these AI-driven tools. articles.summary: Ryan Chaw, a 34-year-old resident of Sacramento, California, has successfully transitioned from being a pharmacist to living off rental income from his diverse portfolio of properties. The...
articles.content: Ryan Chaw, a 34-year-old resident of Sacramento, California, has successfully transitioned from being a pharmacist to living off rental income from his diverse portfolio of properties. The turning point for Chaw came early in life when he witnessed the financial success of his grandfather's real estate investments. Chaw's grandfather had acquired a set of flats in the San Francisco Bay Area at an incredibly low cost during the 1950s. Over time, these properties increased significantly in value and so did the rental income. The substantial returns earned from these investments far surpassed the combined lifetime earnings of his grandparents' salaried jobs. This pivotal experience profoundly impacted Chaw's perspective on wealth creation, leading him to conclude that investing in real estate is an effective way to build generational wealth. He made a conscious decision to adopt this investment strategy and has since expanded his property portfolio. The experience had been a catalyst for Ryan's decision-making process. He'd become fixated on real estate investing after witnessing its potential firsthand. However, entering the world of property ownership was daunting, especially without prior knowledge or experience. Ryan admitted to being hesitant to take action and make a purchase. His father intervened, pointing out the disconnect between his words and actions: "Hey Ryan, you seem to be talking about rentals, but I haven't seen you even contact a real estate agent yet." This rebuke prompted Ryan to take concrete steps towards buying a rental property. He called a local real estate agent on the same day as their conversation and visited several properties in Stockton, California. Location is indeed a crucial factor in real estate, and I made sure to choose properties that would be in high demand. College students tend to prioritize proximity to their classes when searching for housing, so I focused on renting rooms close to campus. My initial experience with marketing was limited, which led to difficulties in filling the first few rooms in my very first year of renting out property. However, after a year of learning from my mistakes, I managed to minimize vacancy rates and maintain a steady flow of renters. Repair costs on my first rental property were substantial, consuming a significant portion of my pharmacist salary. This left me with limited funds to invest in subsequent properties, making it challenging to purchase a second home without borrowing. To mitigate this issue, I had to think outside the box and explore alternative financing options. I was able to secure a mortgage for 10% down on the second property, which was a significant compromise given my initial goal of putting down 20%. However, this decision allowed me to proceed with purchasing the property, albeit at a slightly higher cost. The lender advised me to buy it as a second home, which carried certain tax benefits and also required me to live in the property for a set period. My first five rental properties were all located near the University of Pacific, and I focused on buying investment homes that could generate significant rental income. These properties were rented out by the room, allowing multiple tenants to share the space and increase revenue. By spreading my investments across several properties, I was able to diversify my portfolio and minimize risk. Reading "Rich Dad Poor Dad" had a profound impact on my financial mindset, inspiring me to seek out assets that generate passive income. The book's emphasis on building wealth through smart investing resonated with me, particularly in the context of the FIRE movement, which aims to achieve financial independence by living below one's means and accumulating wealth through investments. After several years of careful planning, I was finally able to replace my pharmacist salary and generate around $10,000 a month from my rental properties, allowing me to feel confident about leaving my job. It took nearly eight years for me to reach this milestone, starting at the end of 2015 and making the decision to resign in August 2023. The process was not without its challenges, particularly with my first home - a 100-year-old property that required frequent repairs due to its age and limited number of bedrooms. I had initially focused on purchasing larger properties, such as those with five or six bedrooms, which tend to generate more cash flow, but I soon realized the potential for higher earnings in other markets. As my grandfather's influence had already instilled in me a taste for investing, I began exploring alternative methods of wealth creation beyond stocks. While the stock market can be a reliable way to build wealth, it doesn't necessarily translate to passive income as easily as real estate does. The allure of rental properties lies in their potential to provide financial freedom in a predictable and consistent manner. articles.title: iPad Pro Faces Competition from Android Tablets with Expandable Storage and Ecosystem Synergy
articles.summary: A new generation of Android tablets offers features like expandable storage and ecosystem synergy with Windows PCs that may appeal to users who don't want to be locked into Apple's ecosystem.
articles.content: The iPad Pro has long been considered one of the most powerful and feature-rich tablets available, but it's not the only game in town for those looking to ditch Apple's ecosystem. Apple's latest flagship tablet boasts an impressive M5 chip, a processor that was previously reserved for laptops like the MacBook Pro. This powerhouse chip is so fast that many users are unlikely to reach its performance limits, making it a top choice for demanding tasks and applications. However, the iPad Pro's locked-down operating system, iPadOS, can be restrictive for some users. The platform only allows apps that have been approved by Apple to be installed, and users must sign into an Apple account to download new software. The iPad Pro's limitations can be particularly frustrating for those who don't own other Apple devices, as the tablet becomes isolated from their existing gadgets and requires workarounds for tasks like syncing files or notifications. Fortunately, there are alternatives available that offer different advantages over the iPad Pro. Many Android tablets offer features like expandable storage and more included accessories, while others prioritize ecosystem synergy with Windows PCs. Windows tablets have also become a viable option, especially now that Windows on ARM is gaining traction. These devices can provide a compelling alternative for those seeking performance without sacrificing compatibility or convenience. The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra stands out from its competitors with its massive 14.6-inch Dynamic AMOLED 2x display, making it a viable option for those seeking a larger screen experience. In comparison to the iPad Pro's larger 13-inch model, this Samsung flagship tablet boasts an even more expansive canvas, ideal for video enthusiasts who crave a cinematic viewing experience. One of the key features that sets the Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra apart from its Android counterparts is its anti-reflective coating, which provides superior visibility in bright environments and eliminates glare. The device's MediaTek Dimensity 9500 processor may not match the iPad Pro's desktop-class Apple M5 chip in terms of raw power, but it still delivers impressive performance for gaming, video editing, and other demanding tasks. The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra's price point is surprisingly competitive with that of the iPad Pro, despite its reduced performance capabilities. Starting at $1,400 for a 256GB model with 12GB of RAM, it gets progressively more expensive from there, topping out at $2,000 for a 1TB model with 16GB of RAM. Amazon's shift in strategy is evident in the new Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, which breaks away from the company's tradition of producing cheap, underpowered tablets. Designed for entertainment and basic tasks, this device now offers a more traditional Android experience, complete with access to the Google Play Store. The key component that Amazon refused to compromise on when designing the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro is its screen, boasting slightly higher pixel density than the iPad Pro's display. Additionally, it features an optional matte coating reminiscent of certain Samsung devices and Apple's iPhone Duo models. A review of the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro revealed that the MediaTek Dimensity 8400 chip inside presented no significant obstacles to productivity or entertainment tasks. However, multitasking did occasionally cause the device to stutter, suggesting a minor performance limitation. The base model of the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro comes with 128GB of storage and an affordable price tag of $500, but it lacks a microSD card expansion slot, which may be a drawback for users who need more storage space. The Nanomatte display is available as an extra feature for an additional $50. The top-spec model of the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, featuring 256GB of storage and including the Nanomatte display, costs $680. This represents a significant price drop compared to other alternatives on the market, making it an attractive option for those looking to switch from the iPad Pro due to budget constraints. The RedMagic Astra 2 offers a powerful Android alternative to the iPad Pro at a lower price point. Its smaller 9-inch screen size may be a drawback for those seeking a larger display, but it's well-suited for gaming where handling is easier. Despite its reduced size, the Astra 2 boasts impressive specs, including the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chip that gives it an edge over other Android tablets. However, its performance still falls short of Apple's M5 chip. The device's cooling system plays a crucial role in maintaining consistent performance. Unlike many top-end Android devices, which throttle their processors to prevent overheating, RedMagic has implemented real liquid cooling and a large vapor chamber to dissipate heat efficiently. RedMagic's Astra 2 also offers several features that set it apart from the iPad Pro. Its display boasts higher pixel density at 313 ppi compared to the iPad Pro's 264, while its 185Hz refresh rate is significantly faster than the iPad Pro's 120. The Astra 2 stands out for its impressive price-to-performance ratio, making it a great option for those looking to save money without sacrificing power. The base model comes with 256GB of storage and 12GB of RAM, all for a relatively affordable $750, while the higher-end configuration offers 512GB of storage and 16GB of RAM for $850. In contrast, Microsoft's Android tablets have some notable features, but they can't match the iPad Pro's level of processing power. For those who require such performance, Windows is likely a more suitable choice than any tablet. The Surface Pro is an intriguing option that offers the full capabilities of Windows 11 on either a Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 Plus or X2 Elite processor. The Surface Pro uses ARM-powered processors, similar to the iPad and offering better battery life compared to traditional x86 laptops. However, this comes at the cost of software support, with many apps not yet optimized for ARM architecture. Before making a purchase, it's essential to check whether your required software is fully compatible with the device. The Surface Pro offers a different user experience compared to iPadOS or Android tablets, as it runs on Windows 11. This can be overwhelming for some users, but professionals who need access to pro-grade software will find it more capable than an Android tablet and potentially even an iPad Pro. The choice ultimately comes down to personal preference, with those familiar with Windows 11 likely finding the Surface Pro a seamless experience. The Surface Pro's complexity is a result of its powerful capabilities, making it a significant departure from other tablets on this list. While it may not be the most intuitive device, professionals who require its level of performance will find it an indispensable tool for their work. The Surface Pro, despite its hefty price tag, offers impressive capabilities that may make it a worthwhile investment for those seeking an iPad Pro alternative. The base model starts at $1,140 for a 12-inch device with 256GB of storage and 12GB of RAM, while the larger 13-inch option begins at $1,200. Upgrading to an OLED screen with a higher refresh rate requires a more powerful processor, specifically the Snapdragon X2 Elite chip. This configuration starts at $1,500 and can reach up to $2,849 for the top-of-the-line model featuring 1TB of storage and 64GB of RAM. articles.content: Petty theft is a risk even in destinations that are considered very safe, highlighting the importance of taking precautions when traveling. Leaving behind flashy jewelry or designer-brand luggage is a crucial first step in minimizing potential losses if theft occurs, as these items often attract unwanted attention. Travelers should also make copies of essential documents and store them securely online, where they can be easily accessed if the physical copies are lost or stolen. Familiarizing oneself with a destination's public transport system is crucial before embarking on a trip. This knowledge can help tourists avoid being preyed upon by thieves who often target transportation hubs in search of unsuspecting visitors. Distracted behavior increases the likelihood of losing one's valuables, making it essential to stay alert and focused while navigating unfamiliar surroundings. Instead of getting absorbed in their phone or other personal items, travelers should keep their gaze up and walk with purpose, allowing them to take in their environment and make the most of their trip. Public transportation is a common hotspot for petty theft, particularly on routes that pass through popular tourist areas like Rome's 64 bus and Lisbon's iconic yellow Tram 28. These vehicles provide an ideal setting for thieves to operate undetected. When using public transport, it's essential to keep bags close and in sight at all times. Travelers should also consider carrying their daypack in a way that makes it difficult for others to access its contents, such as by turning the bag around and wearing it on their chest with the straps looped around their shoulders. When it comes to protecting yourself from petty theft while traveling, even the most secure bags can be vulnerable to skilled thieves. In one instance, a relative of Katie Genter's was targeted on public transportation in Paris - her large purse bag with an open top was easily accessible to pickpockets. To minimize this risk, opt for bags that zip closed and consider clipping the zippers together for added security. Crossbody bags or fanny packs are also less susceptible to snatching than shoulder bags, while a money belt worn under clothing can provide extra peace of mind. As thieves adapt their tactics, travelers must stay one step ahead by investing in better-quality bags. To prevent thieves from snatching items from under your nose, keep a firm grip on valuables like phones or cameras when using them. Investing in a wrist strap or lanyard can help secure these devices, and consider tucking them out of sight when not in use. In public places like hotel lobbies or train cars, take extra steps to secure your belongings: loop your bag strap around chair legs or clip your suitcase to luggage racks. articles.title: Successful People Share One Common Trait: Intense Focus on Work
articles.summary: Business coach Codie Sanchez claims that all successful people she's met share one common trait: an intense focus on their work.
articles.content: Business coach Codie Sanchez claims that all successful people she's met share one common trait: an intense focus on their work. According to Sanchez, who has interviewed numerous billionaires for her podcast BigDeal, this singular obsession is the key to achieving success. Sanchez notes that even though the billionaires she's spoken with are vastly different from one another, they all exhibit a level of dedication that borders on discomfort. "They're obsessed, she emphasizes, underscoring the importance of this quality in driving their achievements. As someone who has navigated both journalism and finance - Sanchez won the prestigious Robert F. Kennedy Journalism Award before transitioning to Wall Street, where she worked for firms like Vanguard and Goldman Sachs - she brings a unique perspective to her work as a business coach. Her credentials are impressive, with millions of followers across various platforms and an estimated net worth of $17 million. Sanchez's approach to empowerment is centered on unconventional paths to financial freedom, such as small-business ownership. Through her company Contrarian Thinking, which also houses a venture fund, she aims to equip people with the knowledge needed to take control of their financial futures. Sanchez argues that entrepreneurs who achieve great success often abandon traditional notions of work-life balance. Their drive to succeed leads them to be consumed by their work, Sanchez claims, making it difficult for others to keep up with their relentless pace. Obsession means that you're constantly thinking and taking action until your efforts become unstoppable," she says. The sheer volume of attempts eventually overcomes any obstacles. This level of dedication is exemplified in the stories of Mark Cuban and Jeff Bezos, who both sacrificed personal time for their businesses. The relentless drive of entrepreneurs like Steve Jobs is a testament to their unwavering commitment to their craft. According to Shalini Govil-Pai, vice president and general manager of Android TV at Google, who has firsthand experience working with Jobs, he would often go into "founder mode," rolling up his sleeves to work closely with the team to seize opportunities. Govil-Pai's observations suggest that even a relatively short period of intense dedication can yield remarkable results. Sanchez notes that three to five years of absolute commitment is enough to achieve significant success, and if this dedication extends to 10 years or more, it can lead to extraordinary outcomes, including the creation of billionaires. Sanchez's statement underscores the notion that success is not solely dependent on a lifetime of dedication. Instead, it highlights the importance of making the most of a short window of opportunity, where sheer volume of attempts eventually overcomes any obstacles, leading to remarkable achievements. articles.title: Pharmaceutical Industry Struggles with New Drug Development Success Rates
articles.summary: The pharmaceutical industry's track record on new drug development is dismal, with over 90% of drugs failing to make it through clinical trials and gain regulatory approval.
articles.content: The pharmaceutical industry's track record on new drug development is dismal, with over 90% of drugs failing to make it through clinical trials and gain regulatory approval. This staggering failure rate underscores the immense challenges companies face in bringing innovative treatments to market. The process from lab to approval can take a decade or more, a timeframe that only adds to the pressure. The industry's struggles are not unique; many sectors experience similar difficulties in converting innovation into success. In consumer tech, for instance, numerous startups have achieved fleeting success before faltering, while automotive companies often find themselves playing catch-up with established leaders in electric vehicles. Retailers investing heavily in digital technologies also frequently struggle to translate these efforts into tangible customer growth. The conventional response to such setbacks is to throw more resources at the problem, including increased funding for projects and a greater emphasis on pursuing novel ideas through acquisitions or internal research and development initiatives. This approach rests on the assumption that innovation's inherent unpredictability can be mitigated by increasing the number of bets being placed. However, this mindset overlooks a fundamental flaw in its logic: simply placing more bets does not automatically lead to better outcomes. A company's success rate is often not directly correlated with the quantity of investments it makes. This disconnect highlights the need for a more nuanced approach to innovation and risk-taking within corporate America. The stark contrast between Vertex Pharmaceuticals' impressive track record in clinical trials, boasting an astonishingly high success rate exceeding 70%, and the industry average of just 10% to 20% underscores this point. The company's executive chairman has recently spoken about how they achieved this remarkable feat, but what are the specific strategies behind their success? Vertex Pharmaceuticals' approach to drug development has been revolutionary in its simplicity: focus on the right target and accuracy becomes secondary. In essence, the company's strategy is akin to entering a darts tournament and throwing at the correct board from the start, rather than trying to hit a bullseye on an incorrect one. By doing so, even if the aim isn't perfect, success is still within reach. The previous emphasis on R&D across multiple programs had yielded few results, with only a single breakthrough product emerging after two decades of investment. This led to a re-evaluation of the company's approach and a shift towards more targeted research. By limiting themselves to diseases with genetically- or pharmacologically-validated targets, Vertex has been able to increase its chances of success significantly. When developing new products, companies often isolate their innovation teams into separate silos, each working towards different goals without considering the bigger picture. This fragmented approach can hinder progress and lead to failure. In contrast, a thriving innovation program requires collaboration between various departments, including research, development, manufacturing, commercial, and regulatory units. These teams must work in harmony from the outset of product development, ensuring that everyone is aligned with the company's overall strategy. To achieve this integration, leaders should involve representatives from all key business units in decision-making processes related to new product development as early as possible. This ensures that everyone is on the same page and working towards a common goal. By breaking down internal silos, companies can streamline their innovation process and increase the chances of success. However, external innovation must also be tightly integrated into the company's strategy, with business development focusing on partnerships and acquisitions that reinforce its existing goals. A company's ability to say no to opportunities that don't align with its strategy is just as crucial as its willingness to take risks. By being selective and focused, companies can accelerate their innovation efforts and achieve better results than those that spread themselves too thin. Innovation is often misunderstood as solely generating ideas, but it's actually about executing them effectively and creating meaningful value for people. The success of an innovative endeavor can breed complacency in companies, leading them to stagnate and fail to push the boundaries further. This was a painful lesson learned by Vertex when one of its breakthrough drugs was swiftly overtaken by a competitor. Being the first to market is no guarantee of long-term dominance; competitors will inevitably learn from your innovations and build upon them. To stay ahead, companies must continually strive to outdo themselves and improve their offerings. Vertex's determination to "out-innovate" itself led to remarkable results, including the development of multiple groundbreaking medicines that have transformed the lives of patients with cystic fibrosis and other debilitating diseases. Our R&D success rate has exceeded 70% across six diseases, a remarkable feat in an industry where the average is 10% to 20%. This achievement was not due to eliminating risk, but rather becoming more deliberate about which risks were worth taking. When evaluating potential projects or investments, leadership teams should ask themselves key questions. Is there a clear understanding of why innovation has failed in similar endeavors before? Are we pursuing opportunities where our unique strengths and advantages can be leveraged? The focus on pipeline size and the number of experiments being conducted is misguided. These metrics measure activity rather than success. True innovators will not be driven by the desire to make the most bets, but rather by a deep understanding of their odds. Innovation requires discipline as much as it does creativity. Companies that sustainably innovate are those that can walk away from opportunities where their chances of success are low. They have the self-awareness to know when to allocate resources effectively and when to cut losses. A remarkable achievement has been reported by Vertex Pharmaceuticals' executive chairman, who attributes the company's success rate in drug trials to its unique approach. By recognizing when to allocate resources effectively and cut losses, they have managed to achieve an impressive 70% success rate - a feat that far surpasses the industry average of 10% to 20%. This exceptional performance is a testament to Vertex's innovative strategy and willingness to take calculated risks in pursuit of breakthroughs. The company's focus on efficient resource allocation has allowed it to maximize its returns, ultimately leading to significant advancements in medical research. As a result, Vertex continues to push the boundaries of what is possible in drug development. Fortune : https://fortune.com/2026/11/22/vertex-leiden-rd-success-rate-fewer-smarter-bets-innovation/

articles.title: Climate Talks Hit Roadblock Over Fossil Fuel References
articles.summary: Negotiators failed to reach consensus on new climate action pledges or how to fulfill previous commitments, with several nations rejecting the proposed agreement.
articles.content: International climate talks in Turkey have hit a roadblock after the European Union and other nations rejected a draft agreement that had effectively eliminated all references to fossil fuels. The breakdown in negotiations came two days short of the scheduled end of the United Nations' COP31 conference, which was attended by delegates from 196 countries and the European Union. Despite the presence of representatives from nearly every country worldwide, the parties were unable to reach a consensus on new climate action pledges or how to fulfill previous commitments. A fourth draft agreement had been put forward in an attempt to bridge the gap between negotiators, but it was ultimately rejected, prompting COP31 President Murat Kurum to admit defeat. Geopolitical tensions reached unprecedented levels at COP31, according to Australian Minister Bowen, who acknowledged the complexity of this year's negotiations. Previous climate conferences had managed to sidestep contentious issues, but this time around, seemingly minor demands became non-negotiable for some countries, causing a stalemate that proved impossible to break. Several nations, including Panama and the Marshall Islands, rejected the proposed agreement, citing its failure to meet the necessary level of ambition in addressing climate change. The second draft of the proposed agreement, released on Thursday, sparked outrage among several nations when it was discovered that all references to fossil fuels had been removed. This move came despite the fact that many countries were pushing for a clear commitment to phase out fossil fuels in order to address climate change effectively. The absence of any mention of fossil fuels in the latest draft has left some countries feeling frustrated and concerned about the lack of ambition in addressing this critical issue. Several countries, including Saudi Arabia, Russia, and India, have been vocal in their opposition to including any reference to phasing out fossil fuels, citing concerns that it could pose a significant financial risk to their economies. The collapse of climate talks at the recent COP31 summit has sparked a sense of urgency and alarm among world leaders. Fossil fuels have emerged as a major point of contention, with several countries opposing any reference to phasing them out due to concerns about financial risks. However, despite this setback, experts warn that inaction will only exacerbate the devastating impacts of climate change, including extreme heatwaves and severe weather events that are expected to intensify significantly. Kurum's options for moving forward include convening a follow-up meeting or delaying decisions until next year's conference hosted by Ethiopia. The history of failed negotiations at international climate summits is not new, with the talks having previously broken down at COP6 in The Hague in 2000. Leaders must now come together to find a solution and make progress on addressing the pressing issue of climate change.
